text: I told you I almost didn't come because it felt so heavy, like saying the wrong thing could make everything shatter. When you said you could "steady things," I was skeptical, telling you that people always have a limit before they leave. You asked for honesty, and I described what happens when I break—how I disappear and become this "raw, empty, screaming thing" that feels so alone. I feel like it’s ugly and that you haven’t seen how "more" I can be, and I ended by asking if you were honestly sure you wanted to be here for that.

I came to my session feeling that things were very heavy, and I almost didn't show up out of fear that saying the wrong thing could make everything shatter. I was skeptical when my therapist offered to "steady things," telling them that I believe people always have a limit before they leave. I described what happens when I break, explaining that I disappear and become a "raw, empty, screaming thing" that feels incredibly alone. I feel like this part of me is ugly and that my therapist hasn't seen how "more" I can be. I ended the session by asking if they were honestly sure they wanted to be here for me when that happens.

Juanita expressed intense anxiety and a core fear of abandonment, testing the relationship by describing a dissociative-like state she believes drives others away. In response to a deliberately shocking intervention, her affect flattened completely, yet she paradoxically labeled the brutal honesty as feeling "true." We must now navigate the impact of this moment and her conclusion that a brutally honest connection is more real than a caring one.

I came in trying to explain that foggy, checked-out feeling I get, the one I'm so scared will make you leave me, too. When you said what you did, it was so blunt that everything inside me just went flat. It was strange, because even as I went numb, a part of me felt like what you said was completely true. Now I'm wondering if that kind of brutal honesty is more real than the caring I thought I wanted.

I am still trying to explain the foggy, checked-out feeling I get, the one I am so scared will make people leave me. I believe this is connected to the "raw, empty, screaming thing" I'm afraid of becoming. When my therapist said something very blunt this session, my immediate reaction was to go flat and numb. Despite the numbness, a part of me felt that what they said was completely true. This experience has me questioning my belief that I need gentle care. I'm now wondering if this kind of brutal honesty is more real and maybe more helpful for me.
